_note: One entry per plugin page. Hotspots are [x %, y %, name, what it lets you do] on the view's image. Every fact comes from docs/<plugin>-manual.md; check there before changing one. Lead crop boxes are [left, top, right, bottom] in % of the image.

groups.name: Dynamics
which: Even out a vocal, bass or drum bus
comp
One compressor over the whole signal, with every control on one page.
Control only the lows or highs of a bus
multicomp
Each band has its own compressor, and untouched bands pass through flat.
Silence a drum mic between hits
gate
It opens on the hit and closes after it, with a filter on what it listens to.
Stop peaks at the end of a master
limit
A brickwall ceiling measured in true peak, with a loudness meter beside it.
Soften “s” sounds, with full control
ds
Threshold, frequency, range and two ways of cutting.
Soften “s” sounds, quickly
ds-mini
One Amount knob on the same engine.

groups.name: Tone
which: Shape the frequencies of a track
eq
Up to 24 bands on a live analyzer, any of which can act only when needed.
Remove steady noise or ringing
fir
It works on the spectrum itself, so it can take out what an EQ can’t.
Add brightness and presence
exciter
It makes new harmonics above a frequency you choose, instead of boosting what’s there.
Add warmth or grit
sature
Four kinds of saturation, at a steady level.
Add low end to a kick
kicker
It swells the kick’s own note, or adds a sub an octave or two below it.

groups.name: Space and time
which: Add echoes in time with the song
delay
Up to 16 taps, each with its own time, feedback and colour.
Put a sound in a real space
verb
It plays the sound through a recording of a room, a hall or a plate.
Add a room or hall you can shape
room
Size, decay and damping move freely, and the tail can freeze.

comp.name: Comp
comp.line: The threshold sits on the input meter, with a filtered detector and a sidechain.
comp.lede: A compressor with its threshold on the input meter, a sidechain, a filtered detector and an output limiter.
hub: For evening out a vocal, a bass or a drum bus, and for anything that needs a sidechain.
Set the threshold right on the input meter
Compress from a sidechain or a filtered detector
Lift quiet passages with upward compression

views.label: Main view
points: Set the level where compression starts, on top of the input meter, so you see what crosses it.
See how much is being turned down, for each channel.
Compress from the track itself or from a sidechain, such as a kick ducking a bass.
Choose how firmly it compresses, and how gradually it starts.
Let the punch through or catch it, and let Auto set the release for you.
Filter what the detector hears, so a bass drum doesn’t pump the whole mix.
Blend compressed and uncompressed sound for parallel compression.
Link the channels, make up the lost level automatically, and limit the output.

views.label: EDIT drawer
views.alt: Fancy Comp with the EDIT drawer open on the Detector page
points: Detector, Character, Upward and Options: the settings you set once and leave.
Shape what the detector hears. Drag the points on the curve, or use the knobs below.
Turn the lows up or down in the detector only, so a bass doesn’t pump the whole mix.
Make the detector more or less sensitive around one frequency.
Turn the highs up or down in the detector only.
Let the threshold follow the input’s long-term level.
Close the drawer and go back to the main controls.

views.alt: Fancy Comp’s Detector page with a bell boost and Auto threshold on

Freq, Gain and Q of the detector’s bell.
On, with the offset from the input’s long-term level and the reference it follows.

views.label: Character

Saturate before the compressor, or after it.
How hard the Character stage is driven.
The saturation curve at the current Type and Drive.

views.label: Upward
views.alt: Fancy Comp’s EDIT drawer on the Upward page

Lift the quiet parts of a performance towards the loud ones.
Limit how far it lifts, and keep it from raising the noise between phrases.
See both directions of compression on one curve, with the lift being applied right now.
The meter keeps showing the threshold in use while you work in the drawer.

views.label: Options

Linear or minimum phase for the oversampling filters.
Exponential, or Linear for a constant dB rate like older compressors.
The detector listens to the compressor’s own output, for a gentler response.
Make Attack the time to reach 90 %, as some compressors quote it.
How strongly linked channels follow the louder one.
The same output level as the header knob.

views.label: Preview filter
views.alt: Fancy Comp with Preview filter on: the title strip says LISTENING
points: The title strip says so while you’re hearing the detector instead of the output.
Hear the filtered detector signal, to set Lowpass and Highpass. It turns off when you close the window.
Set them by ear while previewing.

lead.title: Set the threshold where you can see the signal.
lead.text: The Threshold fader sits on top of the input meter. Pull it down until the peaks cross it, and the GR meter beside it shows what that costs.
lead.alt: The Threshold fader over the input meter, next to the GR meter and the Ratio and Knee knobs

can: Key it from a sidechain input, or from a filtered copy of the track.
Upward compression raises soft passages, with a limit on the lift and a floor under it.
Keep it steady from verse to chorus
Auto threshold follows the input’s long-term level, so the amount of compression stays the same.
A Warm or Bright stage, before or after the compressor, with the curves from Fancy Sature.
A low shelf, a bell and a high shelf on a curve you can drag.
Limit output puts a limiter after the compressor.
Separate Wet and Dry faders, kept in time with each other.

None at the default settings. Pre-comp, oversampling and Limit output add some, and the host compensates for it.

multicomp.name: MultiComp
multicomp.line: Up to 8 bands of compression that sum back flat.
multicomp.lede: A multiband compressor with up to 8 bands. Each band has its own compressor, and the bands sum back flat when they aren’t compressing.
hub: For a bus or a full mix where only part of the spectrum needs control.
Split the signal into up to 8 bands that sum back flat
Drag crossovers and thresholds on the graph
Put a band on Mid or Side only

views.label: Upward compression
views.alt: Fancy MultiComp with the Upward row for band 2
points: Drag a band’s handle down to lower its threshold, and use the mouse wheel on it for the ratio.
Drag the blue lines to move where one band ends and the next begins.
Pick a band to edit, or add one with + for up to 8.
Put the band on Stereo, Left, Right, Mid or Side, hear it alone, or switch it off.
The selected band’s threshold, over its own input meter.
Ratio, knee, attack, release, RMS size and gain for the selected band.
Lift the band’s quiet parts, with a limit on the lift and a floor under it.
Scale every band’s compression and speed together.

views.label: Mid-only band
views.alt: Fancy MultiComp with band 2 on the Mid channel
points: A band on one channel shows its letter on the graph: M for Mid.
Choose the channel the band works on: Stereo, Left, Right, Mid or Side.

views.label: EDIT drawer
points: Make Attack the time to reach 90 % instead of about 63 %.
Automate the crossovers on a log scale, so a sweep moves evenly through the octaves.
The same output level as the header knob.
Up to 10 ms, so the bands start turning down before a transient arrives. The latency it adds is shown below it.

lead.title: Compress only the part of the spectrum that needs it.
lead.text: Each band has its own compressor, and the crossovers sum back flat. Bands that aren’t compressing pass through untouched.
lead.alt: Fancy MultiComp’s band graph with four bands over the spectrum

can: Add or remove bands, and drag the crossovers between them on the graph.
Each band can lift its quiet parts, with a limit and a floor.
Put a band on Stereo, Left, Right, Mid or Side.
Up to 10 ms of lookahead, reported to the host.
Key a band from a sidechain
A band can listen to the sidechain, such as the kick for the low band.
Linkwitz-Riley 24 or 48 dB, or linear phase.
Depth and Time scale every band’s compression and speed together.
details: Mono or stereo, plus a sidechain.
None with the LR crossovers. Linear phase, Limit output and lookahead add some, and the host compensates for it.
pairs: One compressor over the whole signal, with the same upward mode.
After the bands, at the end of the master.
Shape the tone first, then control each band.

gate.name: Gate
gate.line: Closes between hits, ducks from a sidechain and sends MIDI.
gate.lede: A noise gate and ducker with hysteresis, hold, optional 50 ms lookahead, a sidechain input and MIDI triggering.
hub: For drum mics and noisy tracks, and for ducking one track under another.
Close a mic between hits
Look ahead 50 ms so no attack is cut
Send a MIDI note every time it opens

views.label: Main view
points: Set where the gate opens, on top of the input meter, with the closing level shown below it.
Open from the track itself or from a sidechain.
Open 50 ms early, so not even the first transient is cut.
Close on silence, or turn the track down while the sidechain plays.
Watch the level and the gate opening and closing over the last few seconds.
How fast it opens, how long it stays open, and how slowly it closes.
Close only part of the way, so the gate never sounds abrupt.
Filter what it listens to, so only the snare opens a snare mic.
Send a MIDI note on every opening, to trigger a sample.
Blend the gated and ungated sound, and add white noise only while it’s open.

views.label: Sidechain and MIDI
views.alt: Fancy Gate keyed from the sidechain, with Lookahead and MIDI on
points: The gate listens to the sidechain instead of the track.
On: the gate opens 50 ms early, and the plugin reports 50 ms of latency.
A sidechain is chosen but nothing arrives, with a hint on routing it in REAPER.
With Lookahead on, open a few ms before the hit.
Send A4 on channel 1 on every opening, with the velocity from the level.

views.label: Preview filter
views.alt: Fancy Gate with Preview filter on
points: Shown in the title strip while you preview.
Hear what the detector hears, to set Lowpass and Highpass by ear.
Lowpass and Highpass on what the gate listens to.

lead.title: Close a drum mic between hits, and watch it happen.
lead.text: The history shows the level and where the gate opens and closes, so you set Threshold, Hold and Release by eye before you fine-tune by ear.
lead.alt: Fancy Gate’s history, with the gate opening on each hit

can: Turn a track down while another plays, such as music under a voice.
Lowpass and Highpass filter what the detector hears.
50 ms of lookahead opens the gate before the hit.
Hysteresis and Hold keep it from flickering on a decaying note.
Send a MIDI note on every opening, with the velocity from the level if you want it.
Range sets how far it closes, from a few dB to silence.
details: Mono or stereo, plus a sidechain. MIDI out.
None with Lookahead off; 50 ms with it on, at every sample rate.
pairs: Gate the noise out, then compress what’s left.
Gate the kick mic, then give it more low end.

limit.name: Limit
limit.line: Holds a master under a ceiling, with a loudness meter beside it.
limit.lede: A true-peak brickwall limiter with lookahead, three styles, Auto release, a loudness meter and dither, for the end of a mix or a master.
hub: For the end of a mix or a master.
Hold peaks under a true-peak ceiling
Work to a loudness target with the built-in meter
Hear only what the limiter removes

views.label: Main view
points: Clean, Punchy or Dense: how the limiter shapes the peaks it catches.
Pick a loudness target, such as Streaming at -14 LUFS, to aim for.
Pull it down, over the input meter, to push the level into the limiter.
See the input, the output and each reduction in red against the ceiling.
Short-term and integrated loudness, true peak and range, measured as EBU R128 does.
The highest level the output can reach, measured in true peak.
How fast it lets go, and how far ahead it looks.
Catch peaks between samples, and let the release follow the music.
Hear only what the limiter takes away.

views.label: EDIT drawer
points: Off, 2x, 4x or 8x. It sets the latency, not Lookahead.
Off, 16-bit or 24-bit, plain or shaped, for the last bounce.
Show short-term loudness (EBU) or plain RMS on the LUFS bar.
Start the integrated loudness and range again.

lead.title: Reach a loudness target without guessing.
lead.text: The meter beside the history shows the loudness as you pull Threshold down, and the red marks show what each peak costs.
lead.alt: Fancy Limit’s history next to the loudness readings

can: Peaks between samples are caught too, so the ceiling holds after encoding.
Let the release follow the music
Auto release speeds up for short peaks and slows down when the limiting is sustained, which avoids pumping.
Short-term, integrated, true peak and range, beside the history.
Listen to only the limited peaks, to judge how hard you’re pushing.
details: Fixed by the oversampling setting: 318 samples at 48 kHz at the default 4x. The host compensates for it.
pairs: Control each band, then catch the last peaks.
Saturate first for density, then limit.

ds.name: DS
ds.line: Turns down “s” sounds only while they’re too loud.
ds.lede: A de-esser: it turns down “s”, “sh” and “t” sounds in a voice, or harsh highs on cymbals and buses, only while they’re too loud.
hub: For harsh “s”, “sh” and “t” sounds in a voice, or harsh highs on cymbals.
Follow the voice’s level with a relative threshold
Cut only the harsh band, or the whole signal
Watch each cut on the history display

views.label: Main view
points: Set where de-essing starts, over the sibilance meter. Relative follows the voice’s level.
See how far each “s” is turned down.
Listen to the track itself or to a sidechain.
Cut only the harsh band, or turn the whole signal down.
See the sibilance level and every cut over the last few seconds.
Drag the band to where the “s” is harshest.
Where the detection band sits and how wide it is, as a band or a shelf.
How far it can cut, and how fast it reacts.

views.label: EDIT drawer
points: Off, 1, 2 or 5 ms, so the first edge of an “s” is caught.
Minimum phase (no latency) or linear phase (53 ms).

views.label: Listen
points: Shown in the title strip while Listen is on.
Hear only what’s being removed. It turns off when you close the window.

lead.title: Cut each “s” only while it’s too loud.
lead.text: The history shows the sibilance in grey and each cut in green, so you can see that the vowels are left alone.
lead.alt: Fancy DS’s history with a cut on each “s”

can: A relative threshold tracks the voice’s level, so loud and soft phrases are treated the same.
Turn down only the harsh band, or the whole signal for a gentler result.
1, 2 or 5 ms, so the first edge of an “s” is caught.
Listen to only the sibilance being taken out.
Harsh cymbals and bright buses too.
details: Mono or stereo, plus a sidechain for the detector.
None by default. Lookahead adds 1 to 5 ms, and the linear-phase split 53 ms. The host compensates for it.
pairs: The same engine behind one knob, and its settings carry over.
De-ess after the EQ that brightens the voice.

ds-mini.name: DS-Mini
ds-mini.line: The same engine as Fancy DS, behind one knob.
ds-mini.lede: A one-knob de-esser. Pick what you’re de-essing, then turn Amount. It runs the same engine as Fancy DS.
hub: For de-essing a vocal in a few seconds.
De-ess with one knob
Pick a profile that matches the voice or instrument
Move the setting to Fancy DS when you need more control

views.label: Main view
points: Pick what you’re de-essing: Female voice, Male voice, Sibilance, Harshness, Acoustic guitar or Bowed strings.
See the level in the profile’s band and what’s turned down.
The one knob: how much to de-ess.
How far it’s turning down right now.
More settings, including Save as Fancy DS preset.

views.label: EDIT drawer
points: Split cuts only the band; Wide turns the whole signal down.
Off, or 2 ms to catch the first edge of an “s”.
Both channels get the same cut.
Open the same setting in Fancy DS, with every control.

views.label: Listen
points: Shown in the title strip while Listen is on.

lead.title: One knob, set for the voice in front of you.
lead.text: Each profile listens to a different band at a different speed. Pick the one that matches, then turn Amount until the “s” sounds are soft but clear.
lead.alt: Fancy DS-Mini’s profile, display and Amount knob

can: Female voice, Male voice, Sibilance, Harshness, Acoustic guitar and Bowed strings.
Changing profile crossfades over 50 ms, so it never clicks.
Any setting here sounds exactly like Fancy DS set the same way.

Listen to only the sibilance being taken out.

pairs: Every control of the same engine, when one knob isn’t enough.
Compress the vocal, then de-ess what the compression brings up.

eq.name: EQ
eq.line: Up to 24 bands on a live analyzer, with dynamic bands, mid/side and Match.
eq.lede: A parametric EQ with up to 24 bands, draggable handles on a live analyzer, dynamic bands, a channel per band and Match.
hub: For shaping the tone of any track, bus or mix.
Drag bands on a live analyzer
Cut a band only while it’s too loud
Match a track to a reference

Log-scale automated frequency, grid, phase, and Compact mode.

views.label: Dynamic, compact

Off, 2x or 4x, and the selected band’s slope from 6 to 48 dB/oct.
Pre or post, size, window, overlap and which channel it shows.
The graph’s range, a pink tilt so pink noise reads flat, and peak hold.
How slowly the analyzer line moves.

lead.title: Cut a band only while it’s too loud.
lead.text: A dynamic band cuts or boosts only while the level crosses its threshold. The dashed outline shows the most it can cut, and the filled curve what it’s cutting right now.
lead.alt: Fancy EQ’s graph with a dynamic cut on band 2

can: Each with its own shape, from shelves and bells to filters.
Put any band on Mid, Side, Left or Right.
Learn a reference and your material, and Match writes bands that move one towards the other.
A dynamic band can react to another track.
When phase matters more than latency.
Its layout stretches to fill a window of any shape.
details: Mono or stereo, plus a sidechain for dynamic bands and Match.
None in minimum phase with oversampling off. Oversampling and linear phase add some, and the host compensates for it.
pairs: For what an EQ can’t reach: steady noise and ringing.
Shape the tone, then control the level.

fir.name: FIR
fir.line: Removes steady noise and ringing, or draws an EQ freehand.
fir.lede: A spectral processor with six modes: a drawable EQ, Gate, Compressor, noise Subtract, Convolve and Resonance.
hub: For noise, ringing and curves an EQ can’t draw.
Remove steady noise
Turn down resonances only while they ring
Draw an EQ curve freehand

views.label: Resonance mode
views.alt: Fancy FIR in Resonance mode, turning down resonances at 700 Hz and 3 kHz

points: How long Learn listens before it stops by itself.
The same output level as the header knob.

exciter.name: Exciter
exciter.line: Adds brightness above a frequency you choose.
exciter.lede: Fancy Exciter adds brightness and presence: it drives the part of the signal above Freq into a soft clipper to make new harmonics, and mixes them back in.
hub: For a dull vocal, guitar or bus.
Add brightness above a frequency
Make the harmonics denser
Blend it in parallel

views.label: Main view
points: Where the brightness starts: around 2 kHz for presence, 6 to 10 kHz for air.
Drive the clipper harder for denser harmonics.
How much of the new harmonics to add. Nothing changes until you raise it.
How much of the effect you hear.
The level going in and coming out.
Character, the output trim and oversampling.

views.label: EDIT drawer
points: Lean the new harmonics even (warmer) or odd (edgier).
The same output level as the header knob.

lead.title: Add brightness only above the frequency you choose.
lead.text: Instead of boosting the highs that are already there, it makes new harmonics from the part of the signal above Freq.

can: New harmonics, not a louder top end.
Clip Boost drives the clipper harder.
Mix Back sets how much of the effect you hear.
details: Only with oversampling on. The host compensates for it.
pairs: Cut the mud first, then add air.
Catch any “s” sounds the extra brightness brings up.

sature.name: Sature
sature.line: Tape, Tube, Transistor and Clip colour at a steady level.
sature.lede: A saturator with four characters. It adds the warmth or grit of driving tape, valves or transistors without making the track louder, and can keep the lows or the highs clean.
hub: For warmth or grit on a track or a bus.
Choose Tape, Tube, Transistor or Clip
Drive it harder at a steady level
Hear only the added harmonics

Saturate first for density, then limit.

Add a sub an octave or two below
